title: Equidistance Line Finder: The Fair Meeting Line
description: Draw an approximate section of the spherical equidistance locus for two locations; compare surface distances, not travel times.
summary_sentence: The displayed line samples part of the spherical equal-distance locus. It does not account for roads or travel times.
quick_answer: Choose two distinct, non-antipodal places to draw a sampled section of the spherical locus whose points are equally distant from both places. The map interpolates between samples, so the displayed line is approximate.
steps_intro: Two places, one fairness boundary — draw it instead of arguing about it:

body.t: The line can suggest candidate meeting areas with similar surface distances. Check practical road journeys separately — the
calculator gives the centre point itself.
An equal-distance line can provide a geometric starting point for a two-site territory discussion. It does not account for roads, other sites or service capacity.
Draw equidistance lines between several bases pairwise and you are sketching a Voronoi diagram — the geometry behind coverage maps — one honest line at a time.
The perpendicular bisector stops being a compass-and-ruler ritual when it runs between two cities students know. The 'aha' is that the line is a great circle, not a ruler line.
For two selected places, the sampled arc passes through their great-circle midpoint. A location on the arc has approximately equal spherical surface distance to each place.
An equidistant location need not have equal driving times: roads, traffic, borders and transport options differ.

faq: Is every point on the line exactly equidistant?
The calculated samples lie on the spherical equidistance locus; the rendered line interpolates between samples and is approximate.
What is the midpoint used for?
The great-circle midpoint is where the displayed arc crosses the route between the two points. It does not necessarily minimise travel time.
Is the line straight on the map?
The spherical locus is a great circle and can curve in a flat map projection. The tool draws a sampled section.
Does equal distance mean equal travel time?
No — roads differ. The line settles the geographic argument; settle the practical one by testing candidate towns on it with a drive-time tool.
Can I draw lines for three places?
The tool displays one pair at a time. Pairwise lines can help explain the geometry but this workspace does not calculate a three-place solution.
What is this called in mathematics?
The perpendicular bisector of the segment joining the two points — on a sphere, a great circle through the midpoint at right angles to the pair's great circle.
Why does the line extend so far?
The true locus is global, but this tool draws a bounded section around the midpoint, up to 5,000 km in each direction.
